title: Quick check: Debugging Development and Production Differences

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Debugging Development and Production Differences”?
options: The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
Development checks must be checked against the production build and actual deployed environment.
The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
questions.answer_key: Development checks must be checked against the production build and actual deployed environment.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Debugging Development and Production Differences: Development checks must be checked against the production build and actual deployed environment.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying Development checks?
options: Run the production build and test routing, environment config, and monitoring before release.
Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
questions.answer_key: Run the production build and test routing, environment config, and monitoring before release.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Debugging Development and Production Differences: Run the production build and test routing, environment config, and monitoring before release.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before considering “Debugging Development and Production Differences” complete?
options: Check only whether the file exists; syntax and runtime behavior do not matter.
Assume a client-side check proves that a remote service accepted the change.
Rely only on a screenshot of the happy path and never repeat the test.
Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Debugging Development and Production Differences: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
